target.title: fix(agents): preserve primitive tool result output
target.body:
Closes #99523.

## What Problem This Solves

Tools can validly return a primitive string. The visible-output extractor handled only object-shaped content, so a plain string result was silently dropped even though the tool execution completed and the result was available to the handler.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final implementation handles primitive strings at the existing extraction boundary, before object-only block parsing. It reuses the established secret redactor and output cap, replaces syntactically valid inline data URIs with a size-only marker, and preserves ordinary `data:`-prefixed status text. Error classification remains owned by the authoritative `tool_execution_end.isError` event instead of adding a parallel result-object inference path.

## User Impact

Plain-string tool results now appear as visible tool output. Secrets, oversized text, and inline data payloads retain the existing safety boundaries; structured result behavior and event-owned error semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased PR head: `b935a13ccf00b535d102679e57cfb6aba40886dd`.
- Focused behavior proof: 114 helper and handler tests passed, including handler-level emission, secret redaction, truncation, valid data-URI omission, and preservation of non-URI `data:` text.
- Redacted contributor live-Gateway proof observed `primitiveString.visibleOutput=plain result` through the same extraction path; hostnames, addresses, paths, and deployment identifiers were omitted.
- Final structured autoreview: clean, 0.94 correctness confidence after two accepted findings tightened the inline-data boundary and eliminated a `data:` false positive.
- Screenshots are not useful for this nonvisual extraction fix; proof is at the runtime event and visible-output boundaries.

CI is running on the exact head above and will be required green before merge.
